episode_title: HPH403: From landlord to high-performance developer – with David Bradley-Bowles
question: What costs between £1,600 and £2,000 per square metre to build at scale compared to traditional construction?
transcript_excerpt: You can build a passive house at scale between £1,600 per square metre and £2,000 per square metre, which is actually not that much more expensive than a traditional build. This is reasonably achievable and the build costs are not through the roof, though maintaining program speed and consistency without rework is critical to profitability.

episode_title: HPH403: From landlord to high-performance developer – with David Bradley-Bowles
question: Why did David Bradley-Bowles transition from being a landlord to building passive houses?
transcript_excerpt: He got tired of dealing with problems that came out of the woodwork with old homes. He started looking at the blueprint side of things to build first-time good quality stock that would last for the duration of the business, working with investors to fund developments that provided a smoother, slicker system that wasn't just ongoing maintenance all the time. This led him into construction and eventually passive house, which he saw as the right direction for building a robust business suitable for 2030.

episode_title: HPH403: From landlord to high-performance developer – with David Bradley-Bowles
question: What happened to Pure Spring Meadows construction company in 2025?
transcript_excerpt: At the end of 2025, the construction company went into administration. This was linked to the costs of delivering schemes, but was compounded by the fact that the housing market was slow and last year was a quiet year for sales.

episode_title: HPH403: From landlord to high-performance developer – with David Bradley-Bowles
question: What percentage of new build housing in the UK is produced by the five major house builders versus SMEs?
transcript_excerpt: In the UK, 80% of new build housing is done by the five major house builders while only 20% is done by SMEs. This contrasts sharply with Germany, where the market is predominantly 80% made up of SME builders and only 20% made up by big corporates, giving SMEs in Germany much more scope to drive quality metrics in the market.

episode_title: HPH403: From landlord to high-performance developer – with David Bradley-Bowles
question: How did construction costs change between 2019 and 2025 for building projects?
transcript_excerpt: The price of construction in 2019 was 40% down on where it was in 2025, representing a ridiculous rise in costs over six to seven years. This increase was compounded by interest rates going up in 2023, further increases in materials and labour, and scarce land supply with landowners sitting on land rather than selling at market value.
